A1.justification: Both complete 34-page PDFs describe the same CUDA-L1 study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, Appendices A-B, and references support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v7 reports original KernelBench evaluations, cross-GPU experiments, component ablations, and optimization case studies in Sections 4-5.

after.justification: v8 retains these original empirical results, including performance across 250 KernelBench tasks and the ablations in Tables 5, 8, and 9.

M1.justification: The three-stage training pipeline, contrastive prompts, exemplar sampling, GRPO objective, and reward-hacking safeguards in Sections 2-3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use the same 250 KernelBench tasks across three levels and evaluate the same A100, H100, H20, L40, and RTX 3090 hardware scenarios.

E2.justification: Tables 4-6 retain the same reference, Torch Compile, Torch Compile Reduce Overhead, and CUDA Graph comparisons. Table 5 also retains the same vanilla and evolutionary LLM comparators and CUDA-L1 variants.

E3.justification: The 1,000-input correctness check, 30-minute reward measurements, 20-minute evaluation windows, model backbone, and evaluation metrics remain identical.

E4.justification: The training-stage and exemplar-sampling ablations in Table 5, optimization combinations in Tables 8-9, reward-hacking analysis, and case studies are unchanged, including their appendix examples.

E5.justification: Timing repetitions, seven-bucket variance control, and five-attempt best-score reporting for vanilla baselines are unchanged. No seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Tables 4-9 retain their numerical entries and findings. For example, Table 4 reports the same A100 default-baseline mean speedup of 3.12x, median of 1.42x, and 226/250 tasks exceeding 1.01x. The image-based ablation tables are also identical.

T1.justification: The formal definitions and Equations 1-6, covering exemplar sampling, rewards, GRPO, and reward smoothing, are unchanged. No mathematical derivations or proofs are added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about contrastive RL, optimization discovery and combination, benchmark performance, and generalization.

C2.justification: Both retain the same reward-hacking caveats, cross-GPU interpretations, and explanations of CUDA Graphs and mathematical short-circuit optimizations. No substantive qualifications or mechanism arguments change.

D1.justification: The front-page link changes from the project blog to the CUDA-L1 GitHub repository. That repository was already linked in footnote 1 of v7, so this is a limited access-information change, not evidence of newly available resources. Implementation details and appendix code remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Both contain the same 33 references and retain the same positioning relative to evolutionary LLMs, conventional RL, and prior code-optimization research.

P1.justification: The front-page wording changes from 'Project Page' to the repository address, and the version/date text is updated. Body prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The front-page icon changes, and the page-3 code illustration loses its 'Figure 3:' label while retaining its content and explanatory caption. Syntax highlighting changes in Table 2 and Appendix B accompany small spacing and page-break adjustments; scientific displays are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v8 makes an already disclosed repository more prominent and adjusts code highlighting, while removing the Figure 3 label. These limited presentation and navigation changes leave the scientific evidence, reasoning, and substantive reproducibility details unchanged, producing no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
